hints: A path of exactly k flights is a walk, so cities may repeat.
An adjacency matrix entry counts direct flights from i to j.
Matrix multiplication combines one path segment with another; exponentiating the matrix to k gives counts for exactly k edges.
analogy: Compose one-flight route counts repeatedly until the walk has exactly k steps.
example: If 1->2 and 2->3 are the only flights, there is one length-2 route from 1 to 3.
algorithm: Build adjacency matrix A with edge multiplicities. Compute A^k by binary exponentiation under modulo 1e9+7; output entry [1][n].
correctness: By induction, (A^k)[i][j] counts walks of exactly k edges from i to j: matrix multiplication chooses the intermediate city after the first segment.
complexity: O(n^3 log k) time and O(n^2) space for dense matrices.
